content:
Absolutely unbelievable. I asked support to DELETE an old account. They told me deletion would take 14 days. After 14 days, suddenly it was “another 3 days.” Then I was locked out of the account while the actual account remained visible in the game.

Here’s where it gets ridiculous: support then told me the account had been deleted and the data cleared. Except the base was STILL THERE, people could STILL message it, and its Might was STILL CHANGING. How exactly does a “deleted” account keep changing???

I repeatedly asked for a manager/supervisor. Completely ignored. Instead I got generic copy/paste responses telling me the account was deleted, then that what I was seeing was a “temporary display issue,” then that they checked their logs and found “no abnormalities.” I HAVE SCREENSHOTS.

So which is it? Deleted? A display error? A data anomaly? If the data was actually erased, explain how an account that supposedly no longer exists can remain visible and show changing stats.

I spent real money on this account. If you are going to lock a player out, claim their data was deleted, yet leave the account functioning in the game, players deserve an explanation.

And PLEASE don’t reply to this review with another canned “Dear Player” response. Have an actual human being in management review what happened and explain it.

author: BoxOfBees
title: Fine gameplay, awful mismatched graphics
content: Perfectly entertaining gameplay is tarnished by conflicting, unnecessary AI generated visuals. The AI portraits and occasional story graphic are so jarring in comparison to the atmosphere of the game that it’s almost laughable. You’ve got this like, dingy run down plague setting, and the characters fit well when they’re the low poly 3D models. But the second their AI portraits pops up it’s like… wow, that’s John Mobilegame and Jane AI. All the men have exaggerated cartoonish features, which would be fine if it was consistent at all and made with deliberate intention, but it’s not. And the women are genuinely baffling in this setting. Picture the typical AI generated woman, that’s literally it. Uncanny, way too clean for the setting, and NOTHING like the men. The worst part is none of these portraits are necessary. The low poly 3D models are a vibe and they would work just fine on the selection screens, and the talking portraits are unneeded because the text box and character models being on screen more than suffice. The gameplay is fun but so remarkably standard that the only reason you would choose this app over others is the aesthetic and story, but it’s ruined by the lazy addition of AI that completely takes you out of the setting. We need to have better standards, seriously. Put intention and effort into your game, throwing needless AI in there makes you seem like a money hungry tech bro.

author: Root4amber
title: Age related
content:
I enjoy playing Last Asylum and think the gameplay itself is fun and engaging. However, I strongly disagree with the current age rating. In my opinion, this is not a game suitable for children 13 and older due to the unmoderated nature of the in-game chat.

The global and alliance chats frequently contain explicit sexual conversations, profanity, harassment, and other adult content. I’ve also seen server leaders and high-ranking players engage in bullying, targeting, and toxic behavior toward other players, which creates a hostile environment. While not every server is the same, these issues have been common enough that I would not feel comfortable allowing a child to play.

If you’re an adult, you may enjoy the strategy, events, and alliance aspects of the game as I have. But if you’re a parent looking for a game for your child, I would recommend waiting until they’re at least 18 years old or ensuring you can closely monitor their interactions.

The developers have created a fun strategy game, but stronger chat moderation, better reporting tools, and enforcement against harassment would make the community much safer for everyone.
